Serving handler → data layer (request path): FileServerService.serveUserAvatar — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go Profile.AllowAnonymous — internal/profile/profile.go FileServerService.getCurrentUser — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go Authenticator.AuthenticateToUser — server/auth/authenticator.go FileServerService.getUserByUsername — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go Store.GetUser — store/user.go Store.ListUsers — store/user.go Driver.ListUsers — store/driver.go DB.ListUsers — store/db/sqlite/user.go DB.QueryContext — store/db/sqlite/user.go user.avatar_url — store/migration/sqlite/0.11/00__user_avatar.sql Notes: - Route registration: `fileGroup.GET("/users/:identifier/avatar", s.serveUserAvatar)` in `FileServerService.RegisterRoutes` — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go (wired from `server/server.go`). - Auth hops (`getCurrentUser` → `AuthenticateToUser`) run only when `Profile.AllowAnonymous()` is false (private instance). - `GetUser` with a username skips ID cache and delegates to `ListUsers`, which filters `username = ?`. - On Postgres/MySQL, `DB.ListUsers` is the parallel file under `store/db/postgres/user.go` or `store/db/mysql/user.go`; the store interface is the same. - After fetch, `serveUserAvatar` reads `store.User.AvatarURL`, decodes it via `FileServerService.parseDataURI`, and returns bytes with `echo.Context.Blob` — that is response encoding, not additional storage.
